rows.answer: On 2023-06-13 the Panic Index for QQQ sits at 12.29, below the 15 sell threshold and in the 0.6th percentile, so the rule reads it as a greed regime and continues trimming. The rule only adds exposure when the index closes above 64 (panic regime); it only reduces when it closes below 15; anything between 64 and 15 is a hold. So from here, a VIX spike or a collapse in CNN Fear & Greed large enough to push the composite above 64 is the add trigger, while staying at or under 15 keeps the reduce step running until the 0% floor binds. Nothing about price direction alone changes the step — only the composite level at the close.
key_reasons: The latest observation is classified greed with a Panic Index of 12.29 (VIX 14.61, Fear & Greed 79.63, 'extreme greed'), which is below the 15 sell threshold, so the mechanical step on a greed day is a reduction rather than a hold or an add.

The rule's only path to adding is a close above 64: since 2021-05-17 there have been 105 such QQQ panic days, and forward 21-day returns after them averaged 2.4% with a 64.8% win rate — the statistical basis for buying into panic rather than into calm.

Greed days at or below 15 have been far rarer in the same window (7 signal days), and their forward evidence is thin: only 2 completed 5-day windows (mean 1.16%, win rate 50.0%) and no completed 21- or 63-day windows, which is why the tool labels greed a risk-warning rather than a reliable exit.

A neutral print between the two thresholds would stop the sequence entirely — the rule holds when the index is neither above 64 nor below 15 — so the trigger to watch is the composite's level, not the level of any single underlying input.

Fed backdrop as of this date: the 2023-05-03 statement raised the target range to 5 to 5-1/4 percent and said the Committee will determine 'the extent to which additional policy firming may be appropriate' (statement-20230503), and Chair Powell's 2023-02-01 press conference described a step-down to 25bp increases to allow assessment of progress (press_conference-20230201), i.e., a data-dependent stance rather than a pre-announced path.

statements.statement: In the June 14 press conference Chair Powell explained that although nearly all participants expected some further increases by year-end (median dot 5.6% for 2023), the Committee judged it prudent to hold the target range steady to assess how far and how fast policy had already moved; he stressed the decision "was only about this meeting" and that July was live.
statements.reason: Matches press conference: prudent hold, 5.6% median, only about this meeting, July live.

statements.statement: Equity volatility was correspondingly subdued, which is exactly the composition that pins the Composite Panic Index near the bottom of its range.
statements.reason: Evidence does not characterize volatility composition or that it pins the index near bottom.

statements.statement: The Panic Index is a two-input composite (VIX and CNN Fear & Greed); a low reading reflects complacent sentiment, not a forecast, and can persist for long stretches.
statements.reason: Evidence doesn't describe index as two-input composite or persistence claim.

statements.statement: Greed sample sizes are tiny: 11 signal days since 2021-05-17, with no complete 21- or 63-day windows, so greed-day forward returns are effectively unusable as evidence.
statements.reason: 11 greed signal days, no complete 21- or 63-day windows.

statements.statement: Regime days are overlapping exposure days, not independent signals, and forward returns are historical only, not guarantees.
statements.reason: Note states overlapping exposure days and historical, not guaranteed.

statements.statement: Threshold crossings are evaluated on closes; an intraday spike above 64 that reverses by the close would not count.
statements.reason: Evidence says closes but doesn't address intraday spike reversal specifically.

statements.statement: The rule has no sizing beyond fixed ±steps and no stop for a disorderly decline; this is historical research, not investment advice.
statements.reason: Fixed steps, no stop mentioned; not investment advice disclaimer supported.
